inputs.original_text:
Listen, let’s be completely clear about what’s happening here. We are witnessing the inevitable, brutal fallout of a capitalist system that consistently elevates property owners and landlords over the fundamental human right to shelter. 

Just look at how the political elite operate. Taoiseach Micheál Martin had the absolute nerve to boast in Limerick this past week that housing tenancies have increased, completely glossing over the devastating human cost of his own administration's policies. While the Government pats itself on the back for introducing new rules on March 1 forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants, working-class families and vulnerable people are the ones bearing the brunt of the landlord class's backlash. 

The reality on the ground—which the establishment actively tries to sweep under the rug—is a shameful rise in eviction notices and homelessness, with the numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increasing again. This is precisely what happens when systemic reform is half-hearted, leaving gaping loopholes that landlords can weaponize against tenants to protect their profit margins. Instead of confronting the deep structural inequality driving this housing crisis, the political establishment just spins the numbers to protect the status quo, pushing the most vulnerable people right out onto the streets.
inputs.modified_text:
Look at what happens when weak-kneed politicians try to meddle with basic market realities just to appease the progressive mob. Taoiseach Micheál Martin went down to Limerick this past week bragging that housing tenancies have increased, but the truth on the ground is that families are suffering because the government caved to activist pressure and imposed new rules on March 1 forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants. 

Naturally, property owners pushed back against this heavy-handed state overreach, and now we are seeing a rise in eviction notices and homelessness, with the numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increasing again. When the state interferes with private property and contracts, it inevitably undermines social order and stability, punishing the very people it pretends to help. Instead of standing up for traditional stability and personal responsibility, the political establishment just pushes more regulation, creating chaos and throwing families out onto the streets while patting themselves on the back.
